{
  "score": 6,
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh",
      "category": "logic",
      "severity": "medium",
      "line": 1419,
      "message": "The pre-scan concludes 'all complete = all from prior iter' even when some members completed in the current interrupted iteration, causing build to be re-dispatched with stage.start when it should be skipped (DSCMBR-1 violated).",
      "quote": "if [[ \"$_cid_nc\" -eq 0 ]]; then\n            # All complete from prior iter; run all members fresh, emit stage.start for first.\n            _resume_first_iter=false\n            _from_stage_start=true\n        fi",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh",
      "category": "coverage",
      "severity": "medium",
      "line": 276,
      "message": "The DSCMBR-1 test sets `stage_statuses.test = \"aborted\"` rather than `\"complete\"`, so the pre-scan's 'all complete' path (which fires when test has status \"complete\" from iter N-1 and build already completed in iter N) is never exercised; a future regression in that edge case would stay green.",
      "quote": "jq '.stage_statuses.build = \"complete\" | .stage_statuses.test = \"aborted\"' \"$STATE_FILE\" \\",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "test"
    },
    {
      "file": "core/pipeline/runner.sh",
      "category": "logic",
      "severity": "medium",
      "line": 3092,
      "message": "`skip_until_stage` is set to `from_stage` before the dispatch loop, and both cycle:* and stage:* arms clear it only when the matching unit is found; if `--from-stage` names a cycle, the stage:* arm at line 3977 would never see `_ust == skip_until_stage` (stage names ≠ cycle IDs), so `skip_until_stage` is never cleared by the stage:* path and the cycle's own clearing at line 3653 is the only exit — this works, but after the cycle the resume skip guard (`$resume_mode && [[ -z \"$skip_until_stage\" ]]`) activates for all subsequent leaf stages, potentially skipping stages that the user intended to run after the targeted cycle when those stages happen to be marked complete.",
      "quote": "[[ -n \"$from_stage\" ]] && skip_until_stage=\"$from_stage\"",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "design"
    },
    {
      "file": "core/pipeline/runner.sh",
      "category": "logic",
      "severity": "low",
      "line": 3608,
      "message": "The cycle-member artifact check inside the resume skip guard uses `\"${_cyc_id//-/_}\"` to build the `_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_*` var name, while the outer sanitisation for the jq key uses `\"${_cyc_id//[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/}\"` — two different transformations applied to the same `_cyc_id` within a few lines; a cycle ID with characters beyond `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` would look up the wrong var, missing member stages and silently skipping the artifact check.",
      "quote": "local _dc_safe=\"${_cyc_id//-/_}\"",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    },
    {
      "file": "core/pipeline/runner.sh",
      "category": "logic",
      "severity": "low",
      "line": 2026,
      "message": "The temporary `resume_mode=true` override used to skip persona preflight for `--from-stage` is applied before the auto-resume block; if the auto-resume block later resets `resume_mode=false` (e.g., because the state file reports `complete`), the final `--from-stage` validity check at line 2313 fires with `resume_mode=false` and rejects the run with a misleading message ('--from-stage is only valid with --resume') even though the user passed `--resume` explicitly.",
      "quote": "[[ -n \"$from_stage\" ]] && resume_mode=true",
      "introduced": true,
      "fix": "code"
    }
  ]
}
